transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-02-12 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood Solutions); Carlos Mendez (OmniHealth CTO), Aisha Khan (ML Lead), Tom Riley (Platform Eng), Sofia Ruiz (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Customer evaluating open models and deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) for clinical summarization and question answering.
- Primary technical considerations: context length (32k vs 8k), multilingual support (EN, ES), tool-calling / structured output for EHR connectors, and security (SOC2, KMS, VPC).
- Redwood to run benchmarks and share pricing/security docs; schedule POC kickoff.

Topics: model comparisons, context windows, multilingual quality, function/tool calling, deployment tradeoffs (hosted/dedicated/private), security compliance.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Uh, quick intros — I'm Ethan, AE on the GSI account, with Priya our SE.
[00:12] Carlos (OmniHealth): Hey thanks, Carlos here. We'll be talking about models for our clinical autopilot project, so, uh, mainly summarization and question answering over EMR notes.
[00:20] Aisha (ML Lead): Hi — Aisha. Our main unknowns: which open models give the best accuracy on clinical text, and when do we need a longer context window versus chunking. Also cost is big.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. So we'll walk through model options and then deployment modes — rough cost/latency tradeoffs. Quick question: what are the typical doc lengths? Average and tail?
[00:44] Tom (Platform Eng): Average is 8k tokens, but long consults can hit 25–30k tokens, especially consolidated histories. We're trying to avoid heavy client-side chunking if possible.
[00:56] Sofia (PM): And we need Spanish support too — about 20% Spanish notes and some French.
[01:04] Ethan: Okay, so multilingual plus long-context requirements — that suggests we need models with 32k or 64k context variants or infra that can do KV-caching and prefix management.
[01:14] Carlos: On tooling: we need function-calling to hit our EHR connectors — call an endpoint to fetch structured fields, not just free text. Any nuance there?
[01:23] Priya: Yes, function-calling is supported at the API layer — Redwood supports structured tool calls, but there's differences across models: some open models don't have robust function-calling primitives out of the box, so we emulate with structured JSON responses and post-processing.
[01:36] Aisha: Can you say more about differences between Llama-3, Mistral, Falcon and the Redwood verified slightly smaller models?
[01:44] Priya: Sure. High level: Llama-3 variants (esp the 8k and 32k chat optimised) tend to be strong on instruction-following and multilingual; Mistral 7B is very cost effective and surprisingly good on some tasks but needs more prompt engineering for clinical language; Falcon and the big 180B class can be higher quality but much more expensive. Also, model tokenization differences matter for Spanish — some models tokenize Spanish less efficiently which affects cost.
[02:12] Carlos: Do you have numbers on latency for 32k context? Our SLAs are 500–800ms p50 for summaries.
[02:20] Priya: It depends on deployment: hosted CPU/GPU mix will have different tails. On Dedicated with A100s or H100s we can hit p50 ~400–700ms for smaller models with optimized kernels, but large 180B variants at 32k can be in the seconds range. Redwood's runtime has KV cache, continuous batching, etc., but there's a tradeoff: batching improves throughput/cost but increases tail latency.
[02:46] Tom: Is the KV cache per customer or shared? We want to avoid leaking prefixes across tenants.
[02:52] Lena (Redwood Solutions): It's per-tenant, and with Dedicated/Private you can get physical isolation. For Hosted we do multi-tenant but logical isolation and SOC2 controls.
[03:04] Carlos: About private deployments — we have strict PHI rules. Will the private on-prem package integrate with our HSM / KMS?
[03:12] Priya: Yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and on-premised key management; the main difference is you'll run the inference nodes in your VPC or on-prem and Redwood's control plane can be configured for minimal telemetry. There's an additional enterprise license.
[03:28] Aisha: For model selection: how do you recommend we decide between hosted+open model vs Dedicated with quantized large model?
[03:36] Priya: Start with hosted + smaller open models (Mistral 7B, Llama-3-8k) to validate pipelines and accuracy. If you need consistent latency or heavy throughput, move to Dedicated and consider quantized 13–34B models to balance cost/quality. Private is targeted to regulated PHI workloads when you need full control and auditability.
[03:58] Carlos: What about hallucinations in clinical summaries? That's a hard no for us.
[04:03] Ethan: Totally — we focus on grounding via retrieval and tool-calling. Redwood Optimize helps with caching and reranking; we can plug in a retrieval layer so the model only sees context we trust. Also we run evals against prompts to detect regressions.
[04:20] Sofia: Quick question — can function calls return structured outputs that we can deserialize directly into our EHR ingest?
[04:27] Priya: Yes, we support structured JSON outputs. Caveat: depending on model reliability we recommend a validate-and-verify step (schema checks + a small deterministic sanitizer) before writing back to EHR.
[04:39] Aisha: I'd like specifics on multilingual quality — any bench results on Spanish clinical notes?
[04:45] Priya: We don't have OmniHealth-specific tests yet but generally Llama-3 series did well on Spanish in our evals; Mistral sometimes underestimates certain tokens. We'll run a focused benchmark on your sample docs.
[04:58] Carlos: Can Redwood host a dedicated pool with GPU type guarantees? We need predictable p95 latency for batch jobs and online calls.
[05:06] Priya: Yes, Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with autoscale policies. You can choose hardware class (e.g., H100 vs A100) depending on contract. SLA's vary by contract; we can share numbers in the pricing doc.
[05:20] Tom: We may keep most data in our VPC. How's networking handled for private vs dedicated?
[05:26] Lena: Dedicated is still Redwood-managed infra but can be VPC-peered to your environment for private networking paths; Private/on-prem is fully customer-hosted. There's also options for encrypted peering and private endpoints.
[05:40] Carlos: Are there any regulatory blockers with using open models for PHI? E.g., vendor policies or model training data concerns?
[05:48] Ethan: Good question. Open models vary in license and provenance; we recommend an inventory: license checks, opt-out models, and then we do a data governance review. For PHI, Private deployment plus strict KMS and audit logs is our recommended path.
[06:03] Aisha: Benchmark details — what exact measurements will Redwood run? Latency, token cost, exactness of QA, hallucination rate?
[06:11] Priya: We'll run: p50/p95 latency, token cost per request, Rouge/BLEU-style metrics for summaries vs your ground truth, hallucination count on a curated set, and end-to-end wall clock for tool-calls + retrieval. We'll include model size, quantization settings, and batch sizes.
[06:29] Tom: For context longer than native model window, do you stitch with retrieval or do you use Long context models?
[06:36] Priya: Both. Retrieval-first reduces cost; long-context models are simpler but heavier. Our runtime supports prefix/KV caching so repeated prefixes don't re-run, and we support chunking strategies if you want to keep a smaller model.
[06:51] Carlos: Cost example — ballpark cost for a 1k-token summary on Mistral vs Llama-3 vs quantized 13B dedicated?
[06:59] Ethan: Very rough: hosted Mistral might be lowest per token, Llama-3 mid-range, a quantized 13B on Dedicated could end up cheaper at scale due to reserved capacity; we'll put exact numbers in the pricing sheet.
[07:14] Sofia: Function-calling security — can tool calls be proxied through our VPC and audit-logged?
[07:20] Lena: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can route tool-calls through your endpoints and produce audit logs; Hosted can do webhooks with signing and auditing but routing through your VPC requires peering.
[07:33] Aisha: Any gotchas with tokenization differences affecting clinical abbreviations? Like 'BP' or 's/p' tokenizing badly?
[07:40] Priya: Yep that's real — tokenization can split clinical shorthand into multiple tokens and increase cost and sometimes change model behavior. We'll surface tokenization delta in the benchmark report.
[07:51] Carlos: Alright, next steps?
[07:53] Ethan: Recap — Redwood will run the bench on your 10k sample (Priya), send hosted vs dedicated pricing (Ethan), provide security pack + KMS docs (Lena). Customer to share sample docs and target metrics (Tom/Aisha). We'll aim to start POC week of 2025-02-24.
[08:10] Tom: Sounds good. Is there an NDA or legal step first?
[08:14] Ethan: We have a standard pilot agreement; we can attach the pilot SOW to the security pack. If you need an NDA we can get that started too.
[08:22] Sofia: One small ask — can you show a quick demo of function-calling next week? Not full integration, just how structured outputs look.
[08:29] Priya: Yep we can do a 30-minute demo; I'll coordinate with Ethan.
[08:33] Carlos: Great, thanks.
[08:35] Ethan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and booking invite.

End of transcript.
